sentences.text: In today's episode, we are going to talk about how to speak English at school.
If you are studying in an English speaking school or planning to study abroad, you need to know some basic English phrases to help you.
Introduce yourself to teachers and classmates.
Talk about school subjects and schedules.
Speak with the school staff, receptionist, librarian, principal, etc.
By the end of this episode, you will feel more confident speaking English at school.
On your first day at school, you will meet new people.
It is important to know how to introduce yourself and start a conversation.
I am excited to be in this class.
Can you tell me where the science classroom is?
If you don't understand something, you can ask.
Can you speak more slowly, please?
Talking about school subjects and timetable.
Every student talks about school subjects and schedules.
To ask about subjects, you can say, what subjects do you like?
Do we have math class today?
To talk about your favorite subjects, I like English and history.
To ask about the timetable, what time is the next class?
Do we have a test today?

School subjects vocabulary, math, numbers and equations, science, learning about nature, history, learning about the past, English, learning grammar and vocabulary, art, drawing and painting, physical education PE, sports and exercise, asking for help in class.
If you don't understand something, you can ask your teacher or classmates for help.
Can you explain number five again?
How do you say this word?
Can you help me with this question?
What is the answer to number three?
If you don't have something, you can ask.
Do you have an extra notebook?
At lunchtime, at lunchtime, you can practice English by ordering food and talking with friends in the school cafeteria.
To order food in the school cafeteria, can I have a sandwich please?
To talk with friends at lunch.
What did you get for lunch?
Do you want to sit together?
Can you pass the salt please?
Do you have an extra fork?
Where can I get some water?
Here are some phrases to help you ask about them.
If you don't know the rules, ask.
Are we allowed to use phones in class?
Can we eat in the classroom?
Raise your hand to ask a question.
If you are late to class, say, I'm sorry, I'm late.
If you don't have your homework, I forgot my homework.
School is not just about studying.
You can also join clubs, sports teams, and events.
Is there a school trip next week?
Can I join the music club?
If you want to invite a friend, do you want to go to the school dance?
Are you going to the talent show?
If you need information, where is the library?
What time does the school bus leave?
Now, you know how to speak English at school.
Two, ask questions if you don't understand.
Teachers are there to help you.
The more you use it, the better you get.
